tagline: Two loops through the lakes Paul Bunyan stepped in.
intro: The byway is two loops of county road, 54 miles in all, tied together between Pequot Lakes and Crosslake in the lake country about 30 miles north of Brainerd. The lakes, by local account, are Paul Bunyan's footprints, and the shoulders are broad and paved.

The shoulders came first. In 1995 people in Ideal Township, worried about bicyclists on County 16, held a raffle to pay the local share of paving it. Someone from the state tourism office suggested a scenic byway designation might move the job up the county's list. It did, and the shoulders were done in 2002.

moments.title: Pequot Lakes
moments.text: The water tower is painted as Paul Bunyan's fishing bobber, and every July since 1938 Bean Hole Days has cooked beans in pits, in pots with names like Ole and Sven.

moments.title: Breezy Point
moments.text: Wilford Fawcett of the Whiz Bang magazine bought the land here in 1921 for a resort on Pelican Lake, and his own house is now rented out to the public.

moments.title: Crosslake
moments.text: In the Corps of Engineers office south of town sits a Paul Bunyan rag doll nearly 13 feet tall, once a world record holder, in his own wooden chair. He was found on eBay.
